subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what traffic classes should that policy cover across top-level navigation, redirects, subframes, subresources, downloads, and proxy-routed profiles?
rationale: The request creates an operator-trusted browser security/config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent denylist/warnlist boundary or bundled default-list behavior without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define enforceable denylist semantics separately from advisory bot-block warnings before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Let the broader web egress-firewall direction own this only if it explicitly covers browser navigation and browser-specific traffic classes.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable browser denylist and provide only best-effort warnings for known bot-blocked sites.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define enforceable denylist semantics separately from advisory bot-block warnings before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent source-history signal across browser config, docs, and security-sensitive browser-control changes.
